The '''Philip K. Dick Award''' is an American [[List of science fiction awards|science fiction award]] given annually at [[Norwescon]] and sponsored by the [[Philadelphia Science Fiction Society]] and (since 2005) the Philip K. Dick Trust.  Named after [[science fiction]] writer [[Philip K. Dick]], it has been awarded since 1983, the year after his death.  It is awarded to the best original [[paperback]] published each year in the US.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.locusmag.com/SFAwards/Db/Pkd.html|title=Locus index to SF Awards|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090412205849/http://www.locusmag.com/SFAwards/Db/Pkd.html|archive-date=2009-04-12}}</ref>

The award was founded by [[Thomas Disch]] with assistance from [[David G. Hartwell]], [[Paul Williams (Crawdaddy)|Paul S. Williams]], and [[Charles N. Brown]]. As of 2025, it is administered by [[Pat LoBrutto]], John Silbersack, and [[Gordon Van Gelder]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The Official Philip K. Dick Awards Home Page |url=https://www.philipkdickaward.org |website=Philip K. Dick Award |access-date=14 August 2025}}</ref>  Past administrators include [[Algis Budrys]] and David G. Hartwell.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hartwell |first1=David G. |title=The Origin of the Philip K. Dick Award |url=https://www.philipkdickaward.org/2003/03/the_origin_of_t.html |website=Philip K. Dick Award |access-date=14 August 2025 |date=March 6, 2003}}</ref>
